test0_bugReproduction.description: ?buggy=1 (armed guard disabled, exact §4 sketch): single hover move into #target, zero pointerdown events

testA_contextMenuAt500ms.description: pointerdown, hold still (no move) for 550ms wall-clock, then read state

testB_escalateAt1000ms.description: pointerdown, hold still (no move, no release) for 1050ms wall-clock — continuation of the same gesture as test a, run fresh here for a clean timeline

testC_moveAt300msCancelsTimer.description: pointerdown, hold still to 300ms, then move 30px (>8px), then keep waiting to ~700ms to confirm the context-menu timer was actually cancelled and does not fire late

testD_moveAfterMenuFired_observationOnly.description: pointerdown, hold still past 500ms (onContextMenu fires), THEN move 30px, then keep waiting past the 1000ms escalation mark. §4's own comment says this case is undocumented — this is a raw observation, not a pass/fail check.

testE_earlyReleaseClearsBothTimers.description: pointerdown, wait 200ms (under the 500ms context-menu delay), pointerup, then wait 900ms more (past both the 500ms and 1000ms marks from the original pointerdown) to confirm neither timer fires late

testF_overlappingPointerIds_bonusFinding.description: NOT one of tasks a–e. From item-1 code review: dispatch pointerdown(pointerId=1), wait 200ms, dispatch pointerdown(pointerId=2) WITHOUT releasing pointerId=1 first (simulates a second finger touching down while the first is still held), then observe for 1100ms. §4 has no pointerId tracking at all. This is a raw observation of the resulting counts/log, reported as a finding — not fixed here, since none of tasks a–e require it.
